pairs.note: Rate matches (8% p.a., compounded annually), but the answer omits the 100% General Partner catch-up that the key includes as part of the hurdle, and does not state the return accrues on Capital Contributions. The missing full catch-up is a substantive economic element.

Both state a ten-year term running from the Final Closing Date, extendable by up to two successive one-year periods. The key's extra detail (expiry date of December 16, 2034, First Amendment source, and the requirement of prior written consent of a Majority in Interest of the Limited Partners) qualifies but does not change the stated term values.
